title: UCLA working on Bob Chesney contract extension with coach atop hiring boards - CBS Sports
description: Amid a 9-0 start, sources tell CBS Sports that UCLA has been in talks with its first-year coaching star for at le
body:
Amid a 9-0 start, sources tell CBS Sports that UCLA has been in talks with its first-year coaching star for at least a month, as the athletic department confronts debt and sparse attendance
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:26 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The belle of the ball in any coaching cycle would typically be a coach with the profile of Bob Chesney at UCLA, a bona fide young star in the coaching ranks who has taken what is historically thought of as a basketball school to Big Ten and national championship contention immediately. This is a down coaching cycle for now, especially mid-season, compared to the relative insanity of 2025, when there was no true blue-blood job opening besides Florida State. UCLA is certainly working on their end to ensure Chesney is not one-and-done as the Bruins' head man. Sources tell CBS Sports that UCLA is working to sign him to a new deal and has been in dialogue for at least a month. On the heels of Wake Forest getting a new deal done with Jake Dickert, UCLA is working to be the next school to lock in a new deal with its head coach. After Martin Jarmond's departure, Tim Harris is the school's CEO and athletic director. Harris, a UCLA alum, spent three decades with the Lakers, and locking Chesney down would be an important win for the early portion of his tenure. The two sides are optimistic a deal will get done soon, sources told CBS Sports. The Curt Cignetti blueprintSchools have been searching for their version of Curt Cignetti. Coaching cycles have archetypes, and one currently en vogue is the proven winner. 
But there is a difference between hiring a coach who has had a good year or two and hiring someone who has won throughout the ranks, as Cignetti did when he bet on himself to leave Alabama as an assistant in the first portion of Nick Saban's dynasty to go to Division II IUP. He won there, at Elon, James Madison and then ultimately at Indiana, but it was a yeoman's journey up the ladder compared to Ryan Day or Lincoln Riley, whose first head-coaching jobs were at a couple of the most storied programs in the sport's history. Chesney has won at every stop of NCAA-sanctioned college football. He won a conference championship and went 9-2 at Division III Salve Regina. He won two conference titles at Division II Assumption. He won four conference championships at Holy Cross and reached an FCS quarterfinal, and, like Cignetti, he won a conference title at JMU (Chesney's came with a College Football Playoff berth as well). Winners win, as the old adage goes, and in today's college football, schools are more apt to look for coaches who have a track record of success on the field. Of the 16 Power Four conference jobs that opened in 2025, 11 went to coaches who either had head-coaching experience or were head coaches at other schools. A 12th, Ole Miss, went with Pete Golding, who was the interim coach during the team's CFP run. 

        
            
                Troy Aikman calls out 'embarrassing' UCLA attendance as unbeaten Bruins chase CFP berth
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Can UCLA sustain momentum?There is constant conversation about just how serious UCLA is about athletics in general. It's a subplot that never truly goes away around the program. In a letter to UCLA supporters, chancellor Julio Frank wrote: "UCLA Athletics currently carries a significant financial deficit, and its current path is not sustainable." He said the future goal is a model that "supports itself through the revenue it generates."Donor contributions declined every year over the four years preceding Chesney's hire, and part of Harris' task will be to modernize revenue generation.  
Rose Bowl attendance is a constant topic of discussion around the program, as seats sit empty and multiple sections are tarped off in the venerable venue, even as UCLA remains undefeated. Chesney actually addressed it in late October after the team's win against Michigan State, putting the onus on his players to help the effort out by connecting with their classmates to get a better student section.  "The student section was slow to get in there, and then felt like they left a little bit early," Chesney told reporters. "They gotta do a better job too -- we all got to do a better job, but we probably just got to get more involved and make sure our guys in classes are talking about this with everybody...We've done everything we could as far as the tickets, as far as the travel plans and the free access. All those things, I think the administration is doing a great job. We just gotta make sure everybody is talking about it on this campus."UCLA alum Troy Aikman has been more vocal, calling the attendance "a little embarrassing." It's not just the Bruins, as crosstown rivals USC are in the same attendance-discourse boat, but it doesn't help program perception to be wrapped up in it as the team comes down the stretch. 
Any extension for Chesney to keep him in Westwood would likely come with an enhanced package for the roster, and that will be real money to take the Bruins higher than what sources say is a roster over $20 million to match what consistent Big Ten and national title rosters cost, which is around $40 million. Chesney and general manager Darrick Yray have built a roster with some former JMU players, namely star running back Wayne Knight (12, with about six who are significant contributors), and the team has a physical style that has proved to be enough of a platform to help Ty Dieffenbach continue the team's success in the absence of Nico Iamaleava. UCLA is hard at work to prove that the success in Chesney's first year isn't just a blip on the radar, and retaining him will be key to that pursuit.

title: Naz Reid trade rumors: Four NBA contenders that make sense for Hornets forward - CBS Sports
description: After being included in the LaMelo Ball trade, the early part of Reid's tenure in Charlotte has been a bit bumpy
body:
After being included in the LaMelo Ball trade, the early part of Reid's tenure in Charlotte has been a bit bumpy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        You could argue that before this season, there was not a single role player in the NBA more beloved by his own fanbase than Naz Reid. Simply uttering his name, devoid of context, became a popular meme among the Minnesota Timberwolves faithful in recent years, and for good reason. The former undrafted free agent grew into a Sixth Man of the Year winner and one of the best shooting bigs in basketball during his seven-year run with the Timberwolves. Leaving the only team he had ever known this offseason has proven difficult thus far.Reid, 27, is posting big raw numbers in his first season as a full-time starter with the Charlotte Hornets, but there are bigger concerns under the surface. After shooting just under 57% on 2-pointers in Minnesota, he is at around 44% with the Hornets and struggling to score efficiently near the basket. His defense has raised eyebrows as well, and after he was benched in an early game against the Detroit Pistons, Hornets coach Charles Lee said that Reid "didn't meet our standards in the first half, and at halftime we made the decision that he wouldn't play in the second half."
Reid, along with an unprotected 2033 first-round pick, was one of the centerpieces of Charlotte's return in trading star guard LaMelo Ball to Minnesota. The 4-7 Hornets have struggled mightily without Ball, posting the NBA's worst offensive rating this season despite having the league's best offense from early December forward last season. Injuries have played a big part in those struggles, but at this stage, Reid's role as a foundational Hornets player moving forward is already coming into question. Timberwolves beat writer Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic even said on his podcast that the chances of Reid getting traded again are "very high." "The Hornets now are clearly in a period of transition, and they decided that LaMelo Ball was not going to be a part of the team that they believe can eventually get to real contender status," Krawczynski explained. "They made a decision with that core group that they were not good enough as constructed and so they had to take a step back, amass some assets and go forward. And what that also means is that, A, the fans are going to be upset because they finally had a fun season last year and now it is going sideways again, but B, the possibilities of Naz Reid getting traded again are very high. This is a roster that I think is going to change over quite a bit over the next couple of years as the Hornets look for the right combination of people to really vault into what they hope is contention."Krawczynski did not specify a timetable, and we've certainly seen frustrating starts turn into fruitful long-term partnerships, but all of this underlines just how difficult things have been for Reid and the Hornets so far this season. Charlotte knew what it was doing by trading Ball. The idea was to take a step back now to take a bigger step forward later. If that's still the idea here, there should be plenty of teams with real interest in Reid, so let's identify a few possible landing spots for the sweet-shooting big man.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Golden State WarriorsThe Warriors traded for and eventually re-signed Kristaps Porziņģis because they need big men who can shoot in a lineup featuring both Draymond Green and, presumably, Jimmy Butler eventually. Al Horford can cover some of those minutes, but he's 40 and can only be expected to play so much. Fortunately, Green's ability to defend across the positional spectrum means the Warriors don't necessarily need their center-sized shooter to actually defend centers. If he's big, he rebounds and he shoots, he'll fit.
This is Reid to a T. With Green on the team to actually guard the most dangerous centers and the combination of Butler and Yaxel Lendeborg providing size on the wing, the Warriors are fairly well-equipped to minimize Reid's weaknesses. His strengths are exactly what the Warriors need; the not-currently-getting-paid Porziņģis takes Golden State most of the way there when it comes to salary matching (with only a smaller salary like Gui Santos or De'Anthony Melton needed to close the hard cap gap), and the Warriors control almost all of their own future draft capital, so they have the ammunition they'd need to satisfy the Hornets.The big question here -- especially with Stephen Curry now set to miss around a month with an oblique abdominal tear -- is how eager the Warriors are to invest in their present. Before the season, the answer should have been a resounding "not at all." But Curry was playing like an MVP candidate before he got hurt, and the emergence of Lendeborg as the Rookie of the Year favorite has arguably changed the equation. While the Warriors (8-4) may not be able to justify an all-in trade, giving up, say, one unprotected pick to nab the 27-year-old Reid, who can be a part of their post-Curry future as well as their present, might be a satisfactory compromise.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Detroit PistonsThe Pistons have reportedly had an eye on Reid ever since his anticipated 2025 free agency, but he wound up re-signing with Minnesota before the opening bell even rang. The appeal is obvious. Two of Detroit's three best players, Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren, are non-shooters. Having a big man who can shoot theoretically helps offset that deficit, particularly in lineups featuring just one of those two. Detroit tried that very strategy this offseason in acquiring John Collins. The results have been mixed, with the Pistons faring far better in the minutes Collins sits than the ones he plays. Reid is better and younger.
The Pistons are enormously flexible in how they could construct a deal. They control all of their own first-round picks, and they have a fair bit of breathing room beneath the luxury tax. That breathing room evaporates next season, though, when Thompson's rookie extension kicks in. This is where the decision calculus gets harder. Duren and Cade Cunningham are already making market rate. Thompson will be next season, and Duncan Robinson has simply proven too indispensable to move on from. Paying all four of those players plus Reid would leave precious little flexibility to add the second ball-handler Detroit badly needs.Maybe the Pistons feel they're good enough as is to win without one, or they could be prepared to trade someone else out of their core down the line if they feel compelled to seek out that needed ball-handling addition. The Trajan Langdon-led front office is now in its third season at the helm, yet it has not traded a single first-round pick amid Detroit's ascent. The Pistons have been cautious with buy-now moves. Maybe Reid is the sort of player they'd splurge for, but considering how well the Pistons are playing, they will likely be cautious in shaking things up too much. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cleveland CavaliersCleveland's starting five simply hasn't worked this season. The Cavaliers are getting crushed with their five starters on the floor, and the Jarrett Allen-Evan Mobley duo, a frequent target of the rumor mill, is losing its minutes together by over five points per 100 possessions. That duo has never generated the elite rebounding that double-big lineups are supposed to create, and while they do a good job of defending shots at the rim, they give up so many of them that they net out as a fairly underwhelming rim defense. Peyton Watson is struggling to fit in as a small forward, but lineups featuring him and just one of Mobley or Allen are faring far better.
Swapping one of the bigs out for Reid, essentially trading defense for shooting, recalibrates the team in ways that theoretically create a friendlier environment for Watson. The Hornets, still presumably looking for a long-term starter at center, would likely have some degree of interest in either Mobley or Allen. The question is which makes more sense in a trade like this.The answer is probably Allen. He's older. He's worse. He's more traditionally a center than Mobley, whom Cleveland has historically been reluctant to move up from power forward. But the on-off data is pretty clear this season: Cleveland is playing better with Allen on the floor than it is with Mobley. If the Cavaliers are going to go with a single big, it might behoove them to stick with the one they know can be a center. Mobley's 30% max contract is going to prove limiting down the line, especially with Donovan Mitchell starting a 35% supermax deal next season. Mobley would almost certainly net more in a trade than Allen would, and Charlotte has the pick surplus to make a pretty compelling offer if it wants to.If Mobley is available in any way, shape or form by February, offers will come in from several teams. Not many have a package that makes more immediate sense than one built around Reid and Charlotte's picks, which Cleveland could either keep or redirect for other assets. If Cleveland and Charlotte do engage on Reid talks, though, Allen is the far likelier Cavaliers big man to become a Hornet. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Toronto RaptorsWe can't fully judge the Raptors until we see an extended stretch with a healthy Kawhi Leonard, but thus far, Toronto's shooting weakness elsewhere has been as severe as expected. The Raptors rank 24th in 3-point attempt rate and 27th in 3-point percentage as of this writing. Like Golden State, Toronto is perfectly equipped to cover for Reid's deficiencies as a rim protector. There isn't a better trio of defensive forwards in the NBA than Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Collin Murray-Boyles, and Murray-Boyles already plays a reasonable amount of center.The money would presumably be RJ Barrett's expiring contract. Losing his shot-creation would sting, but with a healthy Leonard, they should be covered in that respect. The question is draft compensation. The Raptors already gave up unprotected picks in 2031 and 2033 for Leonard, leaving their 2029 selection as their only tradable, unencumbered pick. They could move their 2027 pick as well, though it has swap rights attached to the Oklahoma City Thunder, limiting its appeal. A swap or two would probably be needed here to seal the deal, but Toronto probably has the chips to pull this off if it's motivated enough. Reid would eat up Toronto's room beneath the luxury tax line next season, but with all of their core players locked in, that shouldn't be much of an issue. The Raptors haven't started their tax clock yet, so a year or two above that line (and still well below the dreaded second apron) seems a small price to pay for a genuine championship contender.

        Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez has won the 2026 American League MVP, the BBWAA announced Thursday night.The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing AL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.Alvarez, 29, bounced back from an injury-riddled disaster in 2025, during which he only played in 48 games. This time around, he avoided the IL and appeared in 158 games. He hit .316/.432/.601 (190 OPS+) with 34 doubles, a triple, 42 home runs, 106 RBI, 105 runs and 6.8 WAR. He made a late run at the Triple Crown, missing out by one home run and seven RBI. He did lead the majors in all three triple slash categories, though, leading in average by five points, on-base percentage by a whopping 42 points -- he led the majors in walks -- and 31 points in slugging percentage. Add the latter two and his OPS victory was 90 points -- 1.033 to second place's .943 (National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong).The only players in MLB history to lead the majors in all three triple slash categories:

title: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh implores NFL to investigate 'loophole' that nixed Daiyan Henley trade - CBS Sports
description: The Broncos and Chargers called off their agreed-upon trade following Henley's physical
body:
The Broncos and Chargers called off their agreed-upon trade following Henley's physical
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The trade that was supposed to send Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos is off. When the Broncos announced that the deal would not be finalized, they did not disclose the reason why the agreement fell apart. But Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh pulled back the curtain and shed light on the negotiations, calling upon the NFL to look into a "loophole" that caused the trade to crumble.Although both teams announced the deal ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, both noted that it was contingent upon Henley completing a physical. It was that examination that led to the trade being called off. According to ESPN, the physical raised concerns inside the Broncos' front office about Henley's knee.Harbaugh said the Broncos used their findings to negotiate trade compensation after the deadline passed. This is permitted, as long as the teams do not add other players to the trade package. The initial deal called for the Broncos to send a 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers in exchange for Henley."The Broncos based a pass/fail on a medical grade based on whether we would take less compensation," Harbaugh said on Thursday after the deal collapsed. "We wouldn't, and we didn't. In my opinion, it's one of those loopholes that the league should really look into, because it sets a bad precedent and continues to set a bad precedent."
Henley has only missed three games in his NFL career and just two (in 2023) due to injury. He was on the injury report in Week 6 with a knee issue but practiced in a limited fashion all three days and participated in that week's game. He appeared again on last week's injury report, but it was due to a shoulder problem rather than another knee ailment, and he practiced in full on Thursday and Friday.Harbaugh said that teams "shouldn't be" allowed to renegotiate trade terms after the deadline regardless of what does or does not come up in physical examinations."That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh said. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."
The picture Harbaugh painted is one where the Broncos were still open to giving up the 2027 fourth-round pick but wanted to reduce the value of the second pick. According to ESPN, Denver proposed a counteroffer of a fourth-rounder and seventh-rounder or a fourth-rounder and a pick swap. The Broncos still reportedly wanted Henley but not at the agreed-upon price."Medical grades should be based on pass/fail, what the medical grade is, not being used by an organization to get less compensation for a trade that was agreed upon," Harbaugh said.Henley was set for a team upgrade himself, as the trade would have sent him from the NFL's only winless squad to the AFC West leader. He has shined individually despite the Chargers' woes and is the team leader in tackles (51) and fumble recoveries (2) and posted two tackles for loss and an interception across his first eight games of the year. Since he joined the starting lineup in 2024, he has been a perennial 100-tackle linebacker and is on pace to cross that threshold again this season.
The Broncos' starting lineup is already set at the inside linebacker spots with Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad occupying the middle of the stout defense, so Henley would have likely arrived as a premier depth option.Henley is in the final year of his rookie contract and will be an unrestricted free agent at the end of the season.

title: UConn forward Nik Khamenia sidelined 6-8 weeks with foot injury as Huskies prepare for tough stretch - CBS Sports

body:
The Duke transfer's absence comes at a brutal time for Dan Hurley, with matchups against Ohio State, No. 12 Arizona and No. 2 Duke looming over the next two weeks
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        UConn will be without starting forward Nik Khamenia for at least 6-8 weeks after the Duke transfer injured his left foot, Huskies coach Dan Hurley announced Thursday. Khamenia suffered the injury midway through the first half of the No. 4 Huskies' 83-41 win over Wagner on Monday night. The sophomore marksman was off to a hot start as the de facto replacement for four-year starter Alex Karaban in UConn's lineup. Khamenia hit his first three 3-point attempts against Wagner and is shooting 61.9% from the floor and 54.5% from 3-point range for the season.Hurley will have no grace period in acclimating his team to life without Khamenia. Up next for UConn is a Friday showdown with Ohio State before a Nov. 18 road game against No. 12 Arizona. After that comes a neutral-site showdown with No. 2 Duke in Las Vegas on Nov. 25.Ranked a five-star prospect in the Class of 2025 by 247Sports, Khamenia came off the bench last season for Duke and averaged 5.7 points on 34% 3-point shooting while logging 19.8 minutes per game. He slotted as a top-40 player during the 2026 transfer cycle and profiled as a potentially perfect fit at UConn.
Khamenia led UConn with 19 points in a 78-70 exhibition win over Michigan State. Even after logging just 10 minutes against Wagner, Khamenia is averaging 10.7 points and is second on the team in made 3-pointers with six behind only Braylon Mullins.Next man up for UConnThe next man up for UConn could be freshman forward Colben Andrew, who is averaging 22.3 minutes per game off the bench. Ranked the No. 26 prospect from the 2026 recruiting class, the 6-6 forward isn't the same caliber of perimeter shooter as Khamenia, but he does a little bit of everything. In 23 minutes against Michigan last Friday, Landrew finished with 14 points, eight rebounds and two assists while helping the Huskies to an 85-77 win over the reigning national champions. Hurley has used a nine-man rotation so far this season. 
Instead of going deep into his bench to keep that number at nine, look for Hurley to deploy an eight-man rotation in the weeks ahead. Given the caliber of opponent ahead on the Huskies' schedule, this isn't the time for experimentation.A regular occurrence for UConnThis marks the fourth straight season in which UConn will have to navigate an extended stretch of schedule without an important newcomer. Mullins missed seven games early last season because of an ankle injury before returning and blossoming into a star.During the 2024-25 season, one-and-done freshman guard Liam McNeeley missed eight games due to an ankle injury. Star freshman Stephon Castle also missed six games for UConn because of a knee injury during its title-winning season in 2023-24.

title: Jake Dickert signs new Wake Forest contract, rebuffing coaching carousel interest - CBS Sports
description: The new long-term deal boosts staff and roster salary pools while shutting down outside interest from open jobs l
body:
The new long-term deal boosts staff and roster salary pools while shutting down outside interest from open jobs like Florida State as the No. 13 Demon Deacons push for an ACC title
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:41 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Wake Forest coach Jake Dickert has agreed to a new contract that will significantly increase his staff and roster salary pools. The new contract keeps Dickert in Winston-Salem long term and rebuffs interest from the biggest jobs on the market. Dickert has done a sensational job at Wake Forest, recording a 17-5 record, including 8-1 this season with the only loss coming against Miami. His 9-4 debut campaign marked the most wins ever by a first-year coach at Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons rank No. 13 in the most recent College Football Playoff Rankings. "Wake Forest University is committed to football success at the highest level and Coach Dickert has done an extraordinary job of inspiring belief among our players, fans and the entire Demon Deacon community," Wake Forest athletic director John Currie said in a statement. "I am grateful for his and Candice's commitment and trust and especially appreciate President Rodriguez and our Board leadership recognizing that now was the time to go ahead and eliminate any outside speculation so that our team and Deacon Nation can put all our energy into the stretch run of this special season."With Dickert secured, eyes will soon turn to offensive coordinator Rob Ezell and quarterback Gio Lopez. Ezell is in his first year as a playcaller at the Power Four level and is leading the No. 9 offense in the sport. Lopez has an 18-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio and the No. 8 QBR nationally. 
No. 13 Wake Forest travels to face SMU on Saturday, with the winner taking over the new favorite to reach the ACC Championship Game against Miami. 
Meteoric riseDickert's rise from a wide receiver at Wisconsin-Stevens Point to a sought-after ACC coach is truly unique. Two years after graduating, he was on staff at North Dakota State as safeties coach and subsequently worked his way up from Division II Augustana and Minnesota State to the FBS. In 2021, he was elevated to interim coach following Nick Rolovich's abrupt dismissal and quickly shepherded Washington State to consistency. Despite dealing with the mess of the collapsing Pac-12, Dickert went 23-20 with the Cougars and helped them reach the Holiday Bowl. 
Now, he's been a sensational stabilizer at Wake Forest, taking them to the next level in the NIL era. Former coach Dave Clawson found consistent success as a developmental coach, and Dickert has taken his culture into 2026. Lopez's sensational runWake Forest quarterback Gio Lopez was a reclamation project after a mediocre season at North Carolina, thrust into a messy situation with Bill Belichick. Since reuniting with Ezell, an assistant during his successful run at South Alabama, Lopez has hit another level. The junior is completing 67% of his passes for 2,176 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception. He also ran for 317 yards and six touchdowns. He ranks top-three in the ACC in nearly every passing category, along with SMU's Kevin Jennings and Miami's Darian Mensah. 
With Dickert locked in, Wake Forest's top priority should be enticing both Ezell and Lopez to stick around. If they do, it will make the Demon Deacons one of the most interesting teams of the offseason. Resetting the coach marketDickert was repeatedly mentioned as a hot name in the coaching carousel after his impressive job at Wake Forest. He was elevated to head coach at Washington State in 2021, ultimately leading the Cougars to an 8-4 record and three bowl games in four years. Because of his newfound ties to the ACC, Dickert was a popular name at Florida State to help solidify the program. With Dickert now off the board, Florida State's search now turns elsewhere, including towards former coach Jimbo Fisher. Duke's Manny Diaz and Arizona State's Kenny Dillingham have also been rumored for the move.

description: How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction
body:
How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders. New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture  in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning.Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here.Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders liveDate: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey)Streaming: Amazon PrimeFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings SportsbookWhen the Commanders have the ballThe Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down.
Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble.The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin, might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run.In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. 
Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams, Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays.When the Giants have the ballThe Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. 
They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. 
When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers, who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields, not Isaiah Likely, has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields.Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles, slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross. The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. 
Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary, who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy.PredictionI don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14

        Utah's trip to Arizona in Week 11 wasn't circled on many schedules before the 2026 college football season began, but the Big 12 matchup is a showdown between ranked teams and has serious College Football Playoff implications. The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech. Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia. The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. 
  Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know  Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. 
However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier: The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). 
Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. Where to watch Utah vs. Arizona live  Date: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 7:30 p.m. ET  Location: Casino Del Sol Stadium -- Tucson, Arizona  TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free)
  Utah vs. Arizona prediction, picks  The Wildcats are a good football team and should provide a big test for the Utes coming off last week's win. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number. Pick: Utah -2.5

        Louisiana basketball's nonconference tilt against UNC-Wilmington on Saturday has been postponed "due to an insufficient number of available student-athletes," the school announced Thursday. The school mentioned that it will try to reschedule the contest.The Ragin' Cajuns only had nine players available in Monday's 56-39 win over Southern New Orleans. Tyshawn Duncan, Deion Ware and the high-flying Todd Jones are injured and have not played this season for Quannas White's club. 6-foot-8 forward Dani Pounds, who scored 15 points in the opening-night loss 75-61 against Akron, missed Monday's game with an illness. That same sickness has apparently spread through the roster, forcing Louisiana to postpone. Louisiana sits 1-2 overall this season with a 67-60 loss to Texas A&M Corpus Christi sandwiched between the Akron defeat and the win over Southern New Orleans.
This is just the second year for White at Louisiana after being one of Kelvin Sampson's top-shelf assistants at Houston for close to a decade. Louisiana went 11-22 and 7-11 in the Sun Belt last season, but a bounceback season was expected. The Ragin' Cajuns were picked sixth in the 2026-27 Sun Belt preseason poll.

It's Week 10 of the NFL season, and for your Fantasy football squads, this is a pivotal week. With more teams on bye and major injuries to starting quarterbacks around the NFL, the fringe plays are now more mainstream and for good reason. Your stat/sit decisons have just gotten a lot more difficult and the matchups play an even more important role now than ever.  That's where Dave Richard's Week 10 matchup breakdown comes in. From defensive coverages and pass-rush pressure to backfield workloads and target distribution, we'll examine the factors that matter most to help you identify trustworthy starters, avoid potential disappointments and make the best possible lineup decisions. Stefon Diggs' playing time hasn't really changed since Terry McLaurin's injury, and he's still been a slot-heavy receiver who is targeted almost exclusively on short routes. However, he and Jayden Daniels have their timing down, as evidenced by his touchdown two weeks ago and a big play last week. Decent target volume is crucial for Diggs against a Giants defense that has improved every week but nickel cornerback Dru Phillips has been up and down all year. Washington's depleted run game plus a competitive matchup should equal north of 32 pass attempts for Daniels, which should put Diggs at a minimum of six targets. He's safe as a No. 3 PPR receiver with some upside to surprise with a good week; Diggs has at least 12.8 PPR points in two of his past three. It's a lack of other reliable running backs that will push you to consider White for Fantasy use in Week 10. He's not close to a full-time back, as he has eight or fewer carries in all but one game this year and doesn't have a game with more than 13 touches. He's also touchdown-dependent -- three of his four double-digit PPR weeks have involved a score. White also ceded the team's lone snap inside the 10-yard line to Austin Ekeler last week and has just 17 snaps and six touches inside the 10 this season (but three touchdowns). Any running back with a better profile, either in terms of workload or explosiveness, is a better pick than White. New York's run defense has looked sharp the past two weeks against Houston and Philly's inferior run games.

Brown, Douglas has at least 15.2 PPR points. The shifty slot receiver not only picks up short throws from Maye but also has connected on 5 of 9 passes of 10-plus air yards in those three Brown-less games. That's roughly half of the overall targets Douglas has gotten from Maye in those matchups. And it's not just Brown who's expected to be out -- Rhamondre Stevenson is also, opening the door for the Patriots to potentially throw a little more than they'd like since they're down to Corey Kiner, Lan Larison and Terrell Jennings at running back. Plus, any offensive line issues will force Maye to get the ball out faster, which can help Douglas pick up more targets. Detroit's pass defense against slot receivers has improved over its past four games just as its overall defense has, but it's been on low pass volume (four targets seen to slot WRs in each of their past two games). It's not a matchup to fear, and it's a good spot for Douglas to keep contributing. A week ago I shared that Jameson Williams was drawing better target numbers than Sam LaPorta in part because LaPorta had been more of a blocker, chipper and check-down option. He'll always do a bunch of that, but last week at Miami was more like the LaPorta we want to see: Between 15 routes on second-and-long and third downs, LaPorta chipped 4 times, blocked once on a designed screen, and lined up away from the O-line 10 times. Sadly, it did not mean a sizable increase in targets, as he had five, marking the fifth time in his past six where he's had that many or fewer targets. The Patriots gave up big games to Brock Bowers and Colston Loveland this season -- both of whom had double-digit targets. Everyone else they've faced had under 8.5 full PPR points and six or fewer targets. Compare that to how wide receivers, especially fast ones, did against the Patriots in 2026, and you can probably imagine where the Lions will aim to attack their opponent this week. I'd be especially concerned about LaPorta having to block and chip a little more against a Patriots pass rush that's nabbed an 8.3% or higher sack rate in each of its past four games. I would expect the Dolphins to try and make things easy for him with quick-game throws; Malik Washington (31%) and Caleb Douglas (24.4%) lead the Dolphins in target-per-route rates on throws under 2.5 seconds and should be on-call here. I just might not expect their targets to be consistently precise. Here's a worry: Green Bay's pass rush has come alive over its past two games, landing at least a 45% pass rush pressure rate in each of its past two games. Granted, they harassed beat-up O-lines from Carolina and New England, but it's still a unit that's gotten hot. The Vikings offensive line has allowed a league-average 36.7% pass rush pressure rate on the year, but that's sort of a byproduct of other Vikings QBs holding the ball too long. By comparison, the Raiders O-line yielded a pressure on 34.1% of its snaps with Cousins, but Cousins also got the ball out on average in 2.62 seconds. I suspect he'll be quick on the draw this week, which should benefit Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson the most. Last point: Only one tight end has scored double-digit PPR points on the Packers all season, but only two tight ends have had six targets against them, so it's not like they've been heavily tested. And the one tight end to do well against Green Bay? That would be Hockenson in Week 1 (4-36-1 stat line). The only quarterback to get more than 15 PPR points against the Vikings defense this season has been Jordan Love, and it took an improbable catch-and-run by Christian Watson in Week 1 to get there. Without that play, Love would have had a bad game, just like Josh Allen, Caleb Williams, Jared Goff, Tyler Shough and other QBs have this season. The problem is that the Packers do not have a capable run game to take pressure off of Love (sorry, Kaleb Johnson's fourth-quarter runs in a blowout win don't count). It means Love will have little choice but to drop back and throw, just as he's done 37.9 times per game this season. That's not a bad thing, especially in the wake of what he did against a good Patriots defense last week, but it's going to be crucial for him to get the ball out really fast. Eleven of his 19 touchdowns this season have come in the red zone on throws under 2.5 seconds, so there shouldn't be much concern about him scoring once he's actually in the red zone. Cover-3 has typically meant great things for Chris Olave (2.97 yards per route run against it), but it's also meant acceptable target volume for New Orleans' running backs and tight ends near or outside the numbers. Easy completions are a big part of Shough's game, and that's how the Saints got Jordyn Tyson involved last week. I suspect he'll play more snaps this week. Keep in mind, Shough lost one red-zone drive on a Tyson fumble, and the Saints settled for field goals on two others. Shough can move this offense. The Saints also play a ton of single-high safety coverage, and against both zone and man concepts, it's been Darren Waller dominating with high target-per-route rates (27.6% versus Cover-3, 24.1% versus Cover-1). New Orleans has let up league-average PPR points to tight ends over their past three games, including a baffling catch-and-run touchdown to Harold Fannin Jr. last week in overtime. Notably, Waller's route rate has ticked up to 67% in each of his past two games, though his targets only shot up last week against Denver (who played Cover-3 and Cover-1 over 50% of their snaps). Waller could minimize the upside for Jalen Coker, though he also has a high yard-per-route average against Cover-3 (2.58 yards). But the Cardinals defense has struggled all year, and now their offense has very little left in terms of experience and explosiveness with rookie Carson Beck starting. title: Cardinals name Carson Beck starting QB: Rookie faces Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett in NFL debut - CBS Sports

body:
Gardner Minshew's season-ending injury opens the door for Beck, whose first assignment comes against one of the NFL's most accomplished pass-rushing duos
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        If the 2026 NFL season feels like an unprecedented year for unheralded rookie quarterbacks, that's because it is. With the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) announcing Carson Beck as their starting quarterback for Week 10 against the Los Angeles Rams (5-4), he will now be the third rookie quarterback drafted outside of the first two rounds to start a game this season. The other two were undrafted rookies -- Jalon Daniels of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Joe Fagnano of the Baltimore Ravens. That hasn't happened since 1987."You never really know until you get to the live bullets on Sunday, but just the way he goes about his business, whether it's been from OTAs through training camp before he got hurt, seeing him operate in that first half," coach Mike LaFleur said. "Plus, the one possession there in the second half, so obviously we'll know more come next Sunday, but we have all the confidence he's ready to roll."Beck started the season low on the depth chart, and reflected on how it feels to move so far up in the same year. 
"Obviously, having gone from the emergency quarterback at the beginning of the season to last week being the backup to now being the starter, it's been a crazy season," Beck said. "It's really been a welcome to the NFL season, just getting introduced to what the league is and what it can be, but I'm super excited for the opportunity and to have the chance to go play with these guys."Jacoby Brissett started the year as the starter, was then benched, and was eventually traded to the Baltimore Ravens. Gardner Minshew took over as QB1 was Brissett was demoted and at that time, Beck was promoted from emergency third quarterback to backup. The Minshew injury now leaves Beck to take over after spending the first half of the season learning from his predecessors. "I think the biggest thing is just watching those two and how they carry themselves and how they handle themselves not only in the meeting room around the coaches, but during the walkthrough, during practice, and during the game," Beck said. "I think that's the biggest thing that you can learn from those guys, of everybody's looking at you as a quarterback, and your attitude has to be right each and every day. The moxie going out there, having confidence, and making everyone around you better."
That "confidence" is not something Beck is worried about. He believes that "confidence is a choice" and having it makes everyone around you better as well. "When you can choose that, again, you just have to go out there and execute," he said. "You have to go out there and do your thing and you have to go out there and be confident, have swag, and have moxie. Regardless of the circumstances, regardless of anything going on around you, regardless of maybe what happened the play before or maybe thinking about what's going to happen the next play. You have to be in the present moment and that's really all you can do and control."To kick off the 2026 preseason, Beck completed 15 of his 19 throws for 188 yards and a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers. Beck will also become the fifth quarterback to make his first career start against a duo of pass rushers with 100-plus sacks each when he faces the Rams' duo of Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. 
"Who do they got?" LaFleur said jokingly. "I got no expectations for him except to go out and play his game one play at a time. Go let it rip, go have some fun. Have some fun with your guys."A depleted group represents Beck's supporting cast, with Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) out for the season and Marvin Harrison Jr. traded to the Houston Texans. Fifth-round rookie Reggie Virgil, undrafted veteran Simi Fehoko and Pro Bowl return man Devin Duvernay are the projected starters. Fortunately, Beck also has the 2025 first-team All-Pro tight end at his disposal in Trey McBride. McBride leads the NFL with 73 catches through Week 9, and he has 11 consecutive games with at least seven catches. Beck also knows a thing or two about feeding his superstar tight end after his years teaming with Brock Bowers at Georgia.

title: Pete Crow-Armstrong wins National League MVP: How will career stack up historically? - CBS Sports
description: Mickey Mantle? Ken Griffey Jr.? Mike Trout? Crow-Armstrong's 2026 season set up the foundation, so let's talk abo
body:
Mickey Mantle? Ken Griffey Jr.? Mike Trout? Crow-Armstrong's 2026 season set up the foundation, so let's talk about the history
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 12, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The MVP winners were revealed Thursday evening and, unsurprisingly, the runaway unanimous winner in the National League was Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs. Crow-Armstrong had an all-time great regular season, which is what the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America award honors. He hit .280/.372/.570 with stellar defense, led the league in home runs (tied with Kyle Schwarber) and massively upgraded his on-base skills. Now, just a few months shy of his 25th birthday, he has an MVP to his name.So what's next? To answer that, we'll look backwards.Since integration, only eight center fielders have posted at least 8.0 WAR in a season age-25 or younger: Willie Mays, Mickey Mantle, Willie Davis, César Cedeño, Ken Griffey Jr., Andruw Jones, Mike Trout and PCA. The only ones to top PCA's 9.8 were Mays, Mantle and Trout. If we went back to pre-integration, Tris Speaker and Ty Cobb were the only others who bested PCA here. What road map will PCA's career follow? The Davis routeWillie Davis was an inconsistent hitter through his age-23 season but had flashed a nice power-speed combo. Sound familiar? That gaudy 8.4 WAR total in 1964, though, was driven largely by monster defensive metrics. Davis hit .294/.316/.413 (110 OPS+) with 23 doubles, seven triples, 12 home runs, 77 RBI, 91 runs and 42 steals. There's little doubt that PCA's 2026 season dwarfed this one overall, and Davis was far behind Mays (11.0) for the league lead in WAR. 
For the rest of his career, Davis averaged 3.1 WAR per season, and though he had good years, he never reached 6.0 WAR again. The WAR figure was, again, mostly driven by defense. He had several good offensive seasons, but his only 20-homer season came in 1962 when he was 22, two years prior to his career year. Davis' career probably looks a lot like PCA's apparent upside before his home run barrage in the first half of 2025. He racked up over 60 career WAR with a decent batting average, excellent defense and excellent baserunning. With PCA reaching 30-30 last year and 40-40 this year, though, the bar has been raised. 
The Jones/Cedeño routeCésar Cedeño followed up his 8.0 WAR season with a 7.4 season at age 22 and 5.8 at age 23. He was very good through age 29 and, in fact, the most statistically similar player through both ages 27 and 28 was Hall of Famer Carl Yastrzemski. Things fell apart after that. As a quick and easy way to illustrate it, Cedeño amassed 49.4 WAR through his age-29 season and only 3.6 in his final six years. It's easier to remember that Andruw Jones' career unfolded in similar fashion because we witnessed it not too long ago and then discussed his Hall of Fame candidacy during his nine turns on the ballot before he finally made it in. In Jones' 12 Braves' season, he racked up 368 home runs, 1,117 RBI and 61 WAR while generally being considered the best defensive center fielder in baseball. Once he left, in time for his age-31 season, Jones accrued just 1.7 WAR in his last five seasons. Through Jones' age-28 season, the most statistically similar players are Bryce Harper and Frank Robinson. 
To compare these two to Crow-Armstrong, the argument would be that he'll continue to look like one of the best players in baseball -- even if taking steps backward from being the very best in the 2026 regular season -- before falling apart once he's around 30 years old. Certainly possible, but given the adjustments he's already not only been willing to make at the plate, but eager to make, I'm just not seeing him all of a sudden hitting a wall. Sure, at some point he'll start losing speed and that'll affect his defensive range and baserunning, but why would the plate skills deteriorate all of a sudden? Then again, few saw it coming with Jones. The Mantle/Trout/Griffey routeAll three of these players were on the path to having an argument as the best player in history before injuries derailed them in their 30s and left them as mere "all-time greats." 
Through Mickey Mantle's age-30 season, he had 90.7 WAR. He averaged 121 games per year in his final six seasons, putting up 19.5 WAR. Through  Ken Griffey Jr.'s age-30 season, he had 76.2 WAR. He played 10 more seasons, but only amassed 7.6 more WAR. Through Mike Trout's age-27 season, he had 72.1 WAR (his top statistical similars were Mantle, Robinson and Griffey). We'll skip 2020 for obvious reasons, but since then he's averaged 90 games and 3.0 WAR per season. Even with the drop-offs, it would be surprising to see Crow-Armstrong reach this level because it's surprising to see any player reach this lofty standard. In career WAR among center fielders, Mantle is fourth, Trout is fifth and Griffey is sixth. They trail only Cobb, Speaker and the guy we're going to discuss next. Joe DiMaggio is seventh. The Mays routeDespite the lofty standard PCA set for himself in 2026, coming close to Willie Mays' career would be jaw-droppingly shocking, and that is absolutely not intended as a slight.
Mays has an argument as the greatest player in baseball history and he put himself in that discussion by being good at everything and doing it all with great longevity. From his age-23 to -35 seasons, he led the majors in WAR eight times, leading the NL an additional two times. His worst seasons in that timeframe were 7.6 and 7.8 WAR. In that span, he also led the league in runs twice, hits once, triples three times, home runs three times, stolen bases four times, average once, on-base percentage once, slugging percentage five times and OPS five times. Mays even posted 5.2 WAR at age 39 and 6.3 at age 40. He led the NL with a .425 OBP when he was 40 years old! He hit .345/.411/.667 at age 23. Mays' 156.2 career WAR ranks third among position players all-time behind two guys you might have heard of: Barry Bonds (162.8) and Babe Ruth (162.3). 
I feel pretty strongly Pete Crow-Armstrong isn't headed for a run at this career and that's just fine. The realistic long-term range for the 2026 National League MVP seems somewhere between Cedeño and Mantle. It's a wide variance of outcomes between those two, obviously, as well it should be when the player we discuss is only 24 years old. For his name to be mentioned among these at all is a testament to the year Crow-Armstrong just put together.
